title: Little Office of S. Francis of Paola, Founder of the Order of Minims
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Sancto Francisco de Paula nascente lux miraculosa in domo resplenduit.
blocks.english: ℣. At the birth of Saint Francis of Paola a miraculous light shone in the house.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Paulae nascentis claritas Noctis illustrat nubila, Canoras fert laetitias Qui docuit silentia,
blocks.english:
The brightness of Paola at his birth
Illumines the darkness of night;
He who taught silence
Brings tuneful joys,

blocks.source: Adam etiam intemperans Noctem tulit nepotibus, Reduxit lucem imperans Carnes caret carinibus;
blocks.english:
Intemperate Adam also
Brought night upon his descendants;
He brought back light by commanding
[The printed “Carnes caret carinibus” is unresolved.]
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Carnes caret carinibus”; its sense is unresolved. The earlier “Reduxit” has an uncertain subject. No missing fasting instruction is invented.

blocks.source: Pulsis dapum vaporibus Nam ut serenat cerebra, Lucidor sic spiritus Per carnis fit jejunia.
blocks.english:
For, as the vapours of feasts are driven away
And the mind is made clear,
So the spirit becomes more luminous
Through fasting of the flesh.
blocks.editorialNote: The source’s comparative “Lucidor” is irregular; “more luminous” is provisional. The compressed first clause is rendered by its readable sense.

blocks.source: Ant. Videsne, quid faciat jejunium? Demonas fugat, pravas cogitationes expellit, cor mundum efficit, et mentem reddit oratorem.
blocks.english: Ant. Seest thou what fasting doth? It puts demons to flight, drives out evil thoughts, makes the heart pure, and renders the mind prayerful.
blocks.editorialNote: “mentem reddit oratorem” is rendered as making the mind prayerful; the metaphor is retained in sense.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Francisce de Paula,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Francis of Paola,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus humilium celsitudo, qui beatum Franciscum confessorem tuum sanctorum gloria sublimasti: tribue, quaesumus, ut ejus meritis et imitatione, promissa humilibus praemia feliciter consequamur. Per Dominum nostrum
blocks.english: O God, exaltation of the humble, who didst raise blessed Francis, Thy Confessor, to the glory of the saints, grant, we beseech Thee, that through his merits and by imitating him we may happily attain the rewards promised to the humble. Through our Lord

blocks.source: etc.
blocks.english: etc.

blocks.source: Sanctus Franciscus de Paula ab ineunte aetate assiduus orator et contemplator divinorum.
blocks.english: Saint Francis of Paola, from his earliest years, an assiduous man of prayer and contemplator of divine things.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Preces fundit et cantica Pios incurvans poplites Tam grata Deo musices, Ipsi gaudent coelites;
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “musices” is grammatically irregular; the rendering of the musical clause is provisional.

blocks.source: Ora veretur spiritu Sublimis inter sydera, Claro virtutum ambitu Jam forte dignus coelis.
blocks.english:
[The printed “Ora veretur spiritu” is unresolved.]
Sublime among the stars,
In the bright compass of virtues,
Now perhaps worthy of heaven.
blocks.editorialNote: “Ora veretur spiritu” is unresolved. The remaining lines are retained without inventing a subject for the first.

blocks.source: Nam sub carnis pondere Recusat corpus deprimi, Astra volavit scandere Mens valet haud difficili.
blocks.english:
For beneath the weight of the flesh
He refuses to let the body be weighed down;
[The printed “Astra volavit scandere” is uncertain.]
His mind is able, with little difficulty.
blocks.editorialNote: “Astra volavit scandere” and “haud difficili” have defective syntax. The first is left uncertain; the final phrase is provisional.

blocks.source: Ant. Qui secundum carnem sunt, quae carnis sunt sapiunt; qui vero secundum spiritum sunt, quae sunt spiritus sentiunt.
blocks.english: Ant. They who are according to the flesh savour the things of the flesh; but they who are according to the spirit perceive the things of the spirit.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Sanctus Franciscus de Paula perpetuus mundi contemnor et carnis domator.
blocks.english: Saint Francis of Paola, a constant contemner of the world and tamer of the flesh.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints the irregular “contemnor”; “contemner” is a provisional reading.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Primo juventae tempore Haerere nugis renuit, Virili mentis robore Circen repulsam conspexit;
Virgo notatus candido Lapillo castimoniae Jam tutus est a sordido Cupidinis tentamine,
blocks.english:
A virgin marked by the white
Stone of chastity,
He is now safe from the foul
Temptation of Cupid,

blocks.source: Blandis rebellis motibus Carnis terit potentiam, Castis puelli moribus Viri jungens prudentiam.
blocks.english:
Resisting enticing movements,
He wears down the power of the flesh,
Joining to the chaste conduct of a boy
The prudence of a man.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “puelli” is irregular; “of a boy” is provisional.

blocks.source: Ant. Et scivi, quia aliter non possem esse continens, nisi Deus det; adii Dominum, et deprecatus sum, ut mihi de sedium suarum afferretur sapientia.
blocks.english: Ant. And I knew that I could not otherwise be continent unless God gave it; I went unto the Lord and besought Him that wisdom might be brought to me from His thrones.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Sanctus Franciscus de Paula decimo tertio aetatis anno, ducente Spiritu Sancto, in eremum secedit.
blocks.english: Saint Francis of Paola, in the thirteenth year of his age, withdraws into the wilderness under the guidance of the Holy Ghost.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Agenti cum triennio Bilustrum nostro juveni Fit sylva pro palatio Sacri doctrix silentii, Eremus, quaeque spernitur A vanis mundi affectibus, Huic coelum et creditur Supernis plenum gaudiis:
blocks.english:
For our youth, when ten years
Together with three had passed,
The forest becomes a palace,
A teacher of holy silence;
And the wilderness which is despised
By the vain affections of the world
Is for him accounted heaven,
Full of joys from on high:

blocks.source: Nec tangitur molestia Remotus a sodalibus, Dei dat suam praesentiam Abstrusus latens specubus.
blocks.english:
Nor is he touched by distress,
Far removed from his companions;
God gives His own presence
To him hidden deep within caves.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Dei dat suam praesentiam” is grammatically defective; the rendering “God gives His own presence” is conjectural.

blocks.source: Ant. In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa: sic in sancto apparuit tibi, ut viderem virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam.
blocks.english: Ant. In a desert land, trackless and without water: thus in the sanctuary he appeared to thee, that I might behold Thy power and Thy glory.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “apparuit tibi,” rather than a standard psalm text. The shift of person is preserved; no external psalm is substituted.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Sanctus Franciscus de Paula annum sexagesimum nonum relicta solitudine ordinem Minimorum instituit.
blocks.english: Saint Francis of Paola, in his sixty-ninth year, leaves solitude and establishes the Order of Minims.
blocks.editorialNote: The historical age is retained as printed; it is not silently corrected from another biography.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Sylvae relictens fructices, Sub Charitatis exercitu Ad bella Christi milites Manu producit strenua,
blocks.english:
Leaving the thickets of the forest,
In the army of charity,
With a vigorous hand he leads forth
Soldiers for the battles of Christ,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “relictens fructices” is irregular; “leaving the thickets” is provisional.

blocks.source: Quem manuevit Charitas, Praedignus hic et signifer, Quo conteratur vanitas, Quam fallax sufflat Lucifer.
blocks.english:
He whom charity has trained
Is a most worthy standard-bearer,
That vanity may be crushed,
Which deceitful Lucifer puffs up.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “manuevit.” “Has trained” is conjectural; the Latin remains unchanged.

blocks.source: Amor tumorem dejicit, Superbiam humilitas, Turgentes vidit ductiles Calore Phoebus nebulas.
blocks.english:
Love casts down swelling pride,
And humility casts down arrogance;
Phoebus beheld the swollen clouds
Made pliant by warmth.

blocks.source: Ant. Charitas non exultatur, non inflatur, non est ambitiosa: sectamini charitatem, aemulamini spiritualia.
blocks.english: Ant. Charity is not exalted, is not puffed up, is not ambitious: pursue charity, be zealous for spiritual things.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “non exultatur”; the literal rendering “is not exalted” is retained instead of substituting a standard biblical text.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Sanctus Franciscus de Paula incomparabile miraculum caritatis.
blocks.english: Saint Francis of Paola, an incomparable miracle of charity.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Ignas domat, et aequora, Terras, flatusque aetheris, Dat lingua mutis organa, Et caecis usum luminis;
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Ignas” and the compressed “Dat lingua mutis organa” are irregular; the English is provisional.

blocks.source: Binis amorum nexibus Tum Numini, tum Proximi Miraclis claret pluribus Aeterno plenus Principi;
blocks.english:
Through the twofold bonds of love,
Both of God and of his neighbour,
He shines with many miracles,
Filled with the eternal Prince;
blocks.editorialNote: “Numini,” “Proximi,” “Miraclis,” and “Aeterno ... Principi” have irregular forms or syntax. The English is provisional.

blocks.source: Nec diligenti potuit Ut Deus quidquam denegat, Quin, quo se plus abjicit, Hoc gratia plus eminet.
blocks.english:
Nor could God deny anything
To him who loved;
Rather, the more he casts himself down,
The more he excels in grace.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Nec diligenti potuit Ut Deus quidquam denegat” is grammatically defective; its English is conjectural.

blocks.source: Ant. Quanto magnus es, humilia te in omnibus, et coram Deo invenies gratiam: quoniam magna potentia Dei, et ab humilibus honoratur.
blocks.english: Ant. The greater thou art, humble thyself in all things, and thou shalt find grace before God: for great is the power of God, and He is honoured by the humble.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Sanctus Franciscus de Paula annum nonagesimum primum die Parasceves moritur.
blocks.english: Saint Francis of Paola dies on Good Friday in his ninety-first year.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Die, qua fudit spiritum Christus in Crucis cathedra Franciscus hoc exilium Perennis intrat gloria,
blocks.english:
On the day when Christ gave up His spirit
Upon the teaching seat of the Cross,
Francis [the printed “hoc exilium” is unresolved]
Enters into everlasting glory,
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “hoc exilium Perennis intrat gloria.” Its connection with exile is unresolved; the readable entrance into glory remains provisional.

blocks.source: Crucem dum tenens, coelici Amoris ictus spiculis, Pendens Jesu vertici Jungi meretur oculis,
blocks.english:
While holding the Cross, struck
By the darts of heavenly love,
[The printed “Pendens Jesu vertici” is unresolved.]
He merits to be joined in sight,
blocks.editorialNote: “Pendens Jesu vertici” has no secure reading. The remaining phrase “Jungi ... oculis” is translated provisionally without completing the defective clause.

blocks.source: Assuetus Christo vivere, Dux vitae postquam mortuus, Cum hoc et vitam cedere Eadem die cupidus.
blocks.english:
Accustomed to live with Christ,
After the Leader of life had died,
He longs likewise to surrender his life
With Him upon the same day.
blocks.editorialNote: “Dux vitae postquam mortuus” has compressed syntax. The relation to Christ’s death is provisional.

blocks.source: Ant. Si enim mortui sumus cum Christo, credimus, quia simul etiam vivemus cum Christo; scientes, quod Christus resurgens ex mortuis jam non moritur.
blocks.english: Ant. For if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live together with Christ; knowing that Christ, rising from the dead, dies now no more.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Sancti Francisci de Paula corpus incorruptum unicum Cruce ab haereticis combustur.
blocks.english: The incorrupt body of Saint Francis of Paola [the printed “unicum Cruce” is unresolved] is burned by heretics.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “unicum Cruce” and “combustur.” The former is unresolved, and “is burned” is a provisional reading of the latter.

blocks.source: ℣. Convertere nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hunc, in quem tumba conditum Formidat marcor furere, Agmen audet haereticum In cineres comburere, Ut, qui tot vivus aspera Abs laurea martyrii Tulit, athletae viscera Jam concrementur mortui,
blocks.english:
Him whom decay fears to assail
As he lies buried in the tomb,
A band of heretics dares
To burn to ashes,
That the body of the dead athlete
May now be consumed,
Who in life bore so many hardships
[The printed “Abs laurea martyrii” is unresolved.]
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Abs laurea martyrii” is unresolved. The metaphor of the dead athlete and the remaining clauses are retained.

blocks.source: Quo rosae, tectae antea Sub castitatis frigore, Amoris tinctae purpura Flagrante furgant corpore.
blocks.english:
That the roses, hidden before
Beneath the coolness of chastity,
Dyed with the purple of love,
May rise from the burning body.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “furgant”; “may rise” is conjectural.

blocks.source: Ant. Qui curavit gentem suam, quasi flos rosarum in diebus vernis, quasi ignis effulgens, et thus redolens in diebus aestivis.
blocks.english: Ant. He who cared for his people, like the flower of roses in the days of spring, like a shining fire and fragrant frankincense in the days of summer.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed reference repeats the indicated prayer group from this office’s Matins; abbreviations within the target are retained.

blocks.source: Francisce! laudes cordibus Has sume fusas intimis, Nuncen orans, coelestibus Ut nosque beet gaudiis.
blocks.english:
Francis, receive these praises
Poured forth from our inmost hearts;
Pray to the Godhead
That He may bless us too with heavenly joys.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Nuncen” is irregular; the reading referring to the Godhead is conjectural.

blocks.source: Humilitatem diligens Supernos inter satrapas Pro Christo dura patiens Jam sedes capis coelicas:
blocks.english:
Loving humility
Among the heavenly rulers,
Suffering hardships for Christ,
Thou dost now obtain heavenly seats:

blocks.source: Comburus qui post funera Levem versus in pulverem, Non sentiens incendia Evehis in martyrem.
blocks.english:
Burned after thy death,
And changed into light dust,
Without feeling the flames,
Thou art raised to the rank of a martyr.
blocks.editorialNote: “Comburus” and “Evehis in martyrem” have defective forms. The English is conjectural; this preserves the source’s devotional claim rather than certifying a historical title.

blocks.source: Ant. Omnia ossa mea dicent: Domine quis similis tibi? eripiens inopem de manu fortiorum, et pauperem a diripientibus eum.
blocks.english: Ant. All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like unto Thee? Delivering the needy from the hand of the stronger, and the poor from those who despoil him.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Francisce de Paula,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Francis of Paola,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus, O sancte Francisce de Paula! mitissimi Jesu humilime imitator, in quo manifeste apparet, humilia Deum respicere, et esse mirabilem in sanctis suis, quique quem paternis intercessionibus beati Francisci Stephani consequum in filium, divina vero providentia in tenera adhuc aetate eduxit, ut humilitationis ac coarctationis solitudinem sponte ingressus, inter asperrimas corporis, animique mortificationes, sexenio ibidem delapseceres, donec adduce divino spiritu progressus faciam, plenamque humilitate Fratrum Minimorum originem fundas; etiam omnibus qua pluries, in summo ignis injectus, sicut nec pedem transgrediens mare, nec amnem innatans, incolumis evasisti, nec innumera illustratus prodigiis; quaesumus, benigne Pater, gloriosae coelorum laetitia! efficaciter apud Deum, ut et nos devoti clientes tui, ab infimo humilitatis gradu ad summum divini amoris culmen pertingere, unaque tecum atque omnibus sanctis, aeternis recreari gaudiis mereamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.english: Let us pray. O Saint Francis of Paola, most humble imitator of the most meek Jesus, in whom it plainly appears that God looks upon the humble and is wonderful in His saints! [The printed clause beginning “quique quem paternis intercessionibus” and naming “Francisci Stephani” is unresolved.] Divine providence brought thee forth while still of tender age, that, willingly entering the solitude of humiliation and restraint, amid the harshest mortifications of body and soul, thou mightest [the printed “sexenio ibidem delapseceres” is uncertain; it refers to six years there]. [The printed clause beginning “donec adduce divino spiritu” is unresolved; it speaks of the founding of the Friars Minims in humility.] [The printed account beginning “etiam omnibus qua pluries” is grammatically defective; it mentions being cast into fire, crossing the sea, swimming a river, and escaping unharmed.] [The printed “nec innumera illustratus prodigiis” is unresolved; it mentions innumerable wonders.] We beseech thee, kindly Father, [the printed “gloriosae coelorum laetitia” is uncertain] effectually before God, that we also, thy devoted clients, may deserve to attain from the lowest degree of humility unto the highest summit of divine love, and together with thee and all the saints to be refreshed with everlasting joys. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The long printed prayer has several unintelligible or grammatically corrupt clauses. Their locations and legible subjects remain marked in English; no historical narrative or missing petition is imported to repair them.

editorialNotes.text: All four printed pages were visually compared. The eight hours, their opening historical meditations, and the commendation remain. The seven “Verse and prayer as above” references expand the printed Matins versicle, response, and collect from this office only. Malformed Latin and historical ages remain as printed; uncertain meanings and corrupt clauses are explicitly provisional or unresolved in English. Abbreviated conclusions remain abbreviated. Hymn line divisions are represented in the prepared English.
